old_row.relationship: All sins moved out of view
old_row.rationale: The psalm asks God to turn His face away from sins and blot out all lawless acts. Isaiah's prayer says God cast all the speaker's sins behind him. Both express removal of all wrongdoing through spatial or erasure language; Isaiah's actual 'behind me' is not changed to 'behind God.'

new_row.relationship: Gathered rulers, trouble and Zion in distinct scenes
new_row.rationale: Psalm 47's kings gather and come together; the next unit reports that they saw, marveled, and were troubled and shaken, with Zion named in verse 3. Psalm 2 has earth's kings stand ready and rulers gather against the Lord and His anointed; God then troubles them, and Zion is named. This assembled-rulers, trouble and Zion pattern is a literary comparison: Psalm 47 does not state the kings' purpose or what they saw, and the assemblies are not identified.
